quests.title: The 5:41 Has No Driver
quests.blurb: I can't put a foot in the door of that thing. So you go. Ride it through to Sydenham, sit at the very front where the cab used to be, and come back and tell me what's there.

steps.label: two flat whites off Restwell Street, his and yours
find the bus stand he still won't look at
ride it to Sydenham with nobody up the front
three eshays reckon the front seat is theirs
photograph the empty cab from the windscreen seat
back to Bankstown and tell him what was there

quests.title: The Deed of Release Says Nothing About You
quests.blurb: Fourteenth pylon from the station end, if they haven't moved it. My name is on it with eleven thousand others. I'm not permitted past the roundabout. The deed says nothing whatsoever about you.

steps.label: take the shuttle off Platform 0 — the one he watches leave
find the volunteer pylons on the Boulevard; count fourteen from the station end
photograph the name, and get the whole pylon in, he'll want the whole pylon in
someone in a lanyard asks who authorised the photography; the second one has a radio
flat white at the Boulevard kiosk, one sugar, on his behalf
back to Lidcombe and tell him what it looked like before you show him

quests.title: Eleven Books Back by Monday
quests.blurb: Every Monday the same eleven books are back in my street library, dog-ears and all, and the bloke who borrows the Bryson says hello like we've never met. Second set of eyes, before I put any of it in writing.

steps.label: be at the counter at 7:40 like the rest of them. same order, same cup, name still spelt wrong
photograph the noticeboard on Erskineville Road. she wants a copy that isn't in her handwriting
three signatures on the noise petition, all of them from the block that went up after the pub
two stops down and see whether it's only Erko doing it, or whether it's the whole line
sixty dollars, earned in front of her. money is the one thing she's sure carries over
read the round back to her at the fence

quests.title: Nobody Puts the Nets Away
quests.blurb: Forty-two Saturdays on the roster and four names on it, and one of the names moved to Queensland. You're doing the coffees, the ground, the poster, the seconds' ice and the book. Then the nets.

steps.label: two flat whites: one for the referee, one for the bloke who becomes the referee if the referee doesn't come
get to the No. 2 ground behind the leagues club. Kickoff is ten. The draw says nine. Both of those are wrong and one of them is Val's fault
the cricket club's working bee has started putting the practice nets up across the wing at ten past ten. Have a word with three of them
photograph the ground at Moore Park for the raffle poster. First prize is a day at the cricket and the poster has said TBC since May
the seconds are away at Kogarah and the gear car is full of witches hats. Take the strapping tape and the ice on the train
sell the rest of the blue book. Ten a ticket, three for twenty, and nobody standing on a sideline in 2026 has cash
back to Val for the last job of the day, which is the job nobody does

quests.title: Notification of the Notification
quests.blurb: The sign has to stand on the fence for fourteen days. It has stood for four, twice. I can't photograph it — council photographing council isn't evidence, it's a diary entry. You can. You're the public.

steps.label: photograph the notification sign on the St Johns Avenue fence, as a member of the public, which is the only qualification the form asks for
three objectors have been harvesting the sign nightly and lodging that it was never displayed; discuss it with them on the verge
raise the $95 lodgement fee, scaled to the cost of works; the works are a hedge
the file lives at the Chatswood annexe, because the Gordon strongroom is being refurbished, and the refurbishment is a development application, and it is being assessed at Gordon
the records counter; ask for it by its file number, never by the address
carry the file back up the hill and hear the determination

quests.title: The Employment Fund Must Be Spent
quests.blurb: There's four hundred and ten dollars in your Employment Fund and it dies Friday. You can't have it. You can have boots, a course, and a ticket to an interview that isn't real. Help me acquit the lot.

steps.label: let the fund pay for the White Card course: six hours, the same slides as the resilience one, a new logo in the corner
collect the steel caps off the loading dock behind Ashfield Mall -- the fund only ever buys size elevens
attend the interview he booked at the far end of the line, because the travel is claimable and the interview is not
photograph yourself in the boots by the Croydon site that has been a hole in the ground for four years -- the audit wants context
the site has views about brand new boots; familiarise yourself with the workplace culture three times
move the surplus: there is a bloke outside the Mall who pays cash for size elevens. Do not say his name in the office.

quests.title: Twelve Weeks, No Grounds
quests.blurb: Forty-one years I've been in this house and the letter says no grounds. It says it like it's a comfort — like the good news is they don't need one. Get me a photo of that back wall before the boy with the roller does.

steps.label: photograph the back wall before the roller gets to it
have a word with the three lads holding rollers
take up room at their open, two doors up
raise the tribunal fee she hasn't got
get to Redfern before the tenants' line shuts
bring her a coffee from the old fruit shop
sit on the step while she reads it out

quests.title: The Same Ute, A New ABN
quests.blurb: Nine floors of waterproofing, done twice, paid for never. The head contractor liquidated on Friday and was trading again on Monday, one stop down the line, new ABN, same ute. Get me a photo of the door.

steps.label: two flat whites before six -- one of them is hers, that is the arrangement
photograph the level nine balcony from Victoria Ave, where the render is still wet
one stop down the line, which is as far as a phoenix has ever had to fly
photograph the serviced-office door: new company name, printed on A4, taped over the old one
have an honest conversation with the three blokes now doing her scope
come back with $120 in your hand, so somebody on this job got paid today
bring the lot back to the hoarding

quests.title: Acceptance Rate
quests.blurb: Three fares stacked, a daughter's assembly at nine, and a rating that dies below ninety. Take the phone, run the queue, and don't let anyone sit in the front.

steps.label: collect the 8:10 from Toongabbie; he is not outside
clear ninety dollars of the stacked queue
two blokes get in the back who never booked it
the app has paused the account; go and see Nav
put the airport fare on the Western line, ride with her
photograph the empty rank for Nav's dispute

quests.title: Was Anyone Else Awake For This
quests.blurb: I need an incident. Westpoint roof, something with a siren in it, and a photo before the police put out their own version. Then get on a train like a sensible person.

steps.label: get up on the Westpoint rooftop, where the laps happen
give the booze bus something to write up
one photo, taken before the police put out their own version
survive the response — all four of them
heat doesn't buy a ticket: all-stops out to Seven Hills
make back what the impound is going to want
tell Ronnie how it went, slowly, she types with one finger
